thread:
alyssa: Heads-up — I reproduced a numerical regression in the new posenc kernel selector path. Happens when the selector picks the ALiBi kernel for long-context inference (seq_len=8192) on fp16. Last ~10 tokens diverge and we get NaNs in the softmax. Posting minimal repro + logs.

vikram: Thanks, can you paste the exact command and model?

alyssa: model: gpt-lite-2
cmd: `python run_infer.py --model gpt-lite-2 --posenc alibi --seq_len 8192 --dtype fp16 --seed 42`
log snippet:
```
RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in exp
attn_scores: [ 1.2e+04  -inf   nan ... ]
softmax produced NaN for head 3
```

sara: saw something similar in nightly earlier. CI attention unit failed on fp16/longctx. It only shows up if slope*pos grows big (positions > ~4096) — looks like exponent overflow in softmax denominator after adding alibi bias.

max: CI log (short): `posenc_stability/attn_overflow TEST FAILED — NaN detected in attn_probs` — reproduced on linux-gpu-4.23.

ci-bot: test posenc_stability/attn_overflow failed on g4dn:09, reproducer attached.

jeremy: hypothesis: ALiBi adds a linear bias proportional to position index. When raw dot-products are already large (fp16 range), adding a large positive bias pushes exp(logit) to inf. Mitigations: 1) cast logits to fp32 before softmax; 2) clamp logits to a safe range (e.g. [-80, 80]); 3) scale down ALiBi slope for long positions; 4) prefer fp32 accumulators in the kernel.

alyssa: quick local patch = cast logits -> fp32 before softmax + clamp to [-88, 88] — fixed the reproducer. Perf hit is small but measurable. Will open PR.

vikram: we need a proper fix strategy rather than just a bandaid. Action items: add guarded cast+clamp behind a flag, add regression test, and evaluate perf. Also consider kernel selector changes: prefer the ROPE-ordered accumulation kernel for cases where ALiBi slope*pos > threshold.

sara: note — ROPE path avoided overflow in our earlier tests because accumulation ordering + fused softmax used a different numeric pattern (and we used fp32 accumulators there). So the behavior difference is implementation-dependent, not algorithmic. We should codify numeric contract for attention kernels.

max: propose tests: (1) randomized stress test seedset for seq_len in {4096,8192,16384} with dtype fp16, check finite outputs; (2) deterministic unit that asserts no NaNs for worst-case slope. I'll add to nightly.

jeremy: perf & rollout plan: put the guarded cast+clamp behind a runtime knob, default on for long seq fp16. Run perf diff on our perf cluster (vikram + jeremy). If perf hit <10% we can keep default-on and follow up with optimized fp32-accum kernel to recover perf.

alyssa: I'll open PR with the guard + patch tests. Early numbers: local microbench (seq=8192, bs=1) shows ~6% slower for the clamp path, but stable. I'll attach benchmark script to the PR.

ci-bot: PR #1421 created by alyssa — https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1421 :party: 

vikram: assigning owners: alyssa (fix + PR), max (tests), jeremy (perf), sara (correctness baseline). ETA: EOW for PR + tests.

jeremy: one more idea — kernel selector should expose a "numeric-safety" score computed from {dtype, seq_len, max_abs_logit_estimate} and choose the more numerically stable kernel when score > threshold. We'll sketch that in the RFC follow-up.

alyssa: noted. I'll add a short section in the PR description describing selector heuristics and a small reproducer harness.

max: :thumbsup:

alyssa: thanks all — will update thread when PR lands.
